year.label: JRM World RX Mini Countryman era

identity.real_world_identity_notes: AMS2 names the car generically as MINI Countryman R60 RX. FIA classifications establish JRM's BMW MINI entry in the 2016 World Rallycross Championship, while the applicable SuperCar regulations establish dog-engagement construction. The exact season, chassis, livery and gearbox unit represented in AMS2 are not established.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was observed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. The current two-stage downshift test found no automatic blip and the gear engaged without pedal input.
An older pre-fix drive reported automatic blip yes; both the corrected isolated recheck and this newer full drive returned no.
The FIA rules establish dogbox construction for the SuperCar but not the exact AMS2 shift behavior; no real-world automatic-blip conclusion is inferred from their silence.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mini-countryman-r60-rx.20260822t040247960z-0ad241fd by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: The exact AMS2 identity and controls were observed live, and official FIA material establishes the World RX Mini context. The simulator's generic name does not identify one exact real build.

claims.basis: The official AMS2 RX catalogue names MINI Countryman R60 RX, and the FIA's 2016 classifications identify JRM's BMW MINI World RX entry. The exact represented season and chassis remain unknown.

The current guided drive selected six forward gears through a sequential stick. FIA Article 279 permits at most six forward gears and permits a sequential layout, so the drive rather than the rule establishes those two values. The rule separately requires dog engagement and prohibits synchronisers and secondary clutch mechanisms, establishing dogbox construction for the SuperCar. It does not establish clutch technique, the cut in this implementation, or downshift blipping.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: FIA Article 279 requires dog engagement and prohibits synchronisers and secondary clutch mechanisms for the SuperCar, establishing dogbox construction. The closest archetype instead carries gearbox_type sequential; the guided drive separately establishes the sequential-stick mechanism.

driver_summary: Six-speed sequential stick in AMS2. Use the clutch to launch; it accepts flat clutchless upshifts and coast downshifts without pedal work, and the corrected drives found no automatic blip.
